tasks.prompt: Fix setDirection so fractional, non-finite, and non-unit inputs are ignored without overwriting a previously queued valid direction, while valid cardinal turns and reversal protection keep working. Implementation: add a failing regression test in test/game.test.js asserting that after queueing a valid direction, feeding (0.5,0.5), (NaN,0), (Infinity,0), and (1,1) leaves the queued direction unchanged; then fix setDirection in game.js by requiring Number.isInteger(dx) && Number.isInteger(dy) before the existing Manhattan-length-1 and isOpposite checks. Assertions: the regression test plus a task-specific behavioral check verifying getState().direction does not change after invalid inputs following a valid turn, and that a valid turn still applies. Verification: run npm test (project check) and the task-specific behavioral check; obtain independent review before handing off to Task 2.
tasks.title: Task 1 — cardinal-unit-vector movement validation
tasks.acceptance: After game.start() and game.setDirection(0,-1) (valid up), calls to setDirection(0.5,0.5), setDirection(NaN,0), setDirection(Infinity,0), setDirection(1,1), and setDirection(0,0) must not change the queued direction: a subsequent game.step() moves the head up by exactly one cell (newY = oldY - 1). Reversal protection (setDirection(-1,0) while moving right) still rejects and the snake keeps moving right; a valid turn (setDirection(0,-1) while moving right) still applies and the head moves up.
tasks.current: In game.js setDirection (around line 120): the guard `if (Math.abs(dx) + Math.abs(dy) !== 1) return;` admits fractional diagonal vectors such as (0.5, 0.5) because 0.5+0.5===1, so `this.nextDirection` is overwritten to [0.5,0.5]. NaN/Infinity inputs happen to be rejected (their sum is NaN/Infinity, not 1), and the isOpposite reversal check works against this.direction. The existing test 'rejects instant reversal into the neck' passes. Unknown: whether any UI caller relies on fractional inputs (ui.js only sends ±1/0 from DIRECTIONS, swipes, and d-pad buttons, so no), confirming the fix is safe.

tasks.prompt: Fix loadBest so fractional, negative, non-finite, and malformed stored best-score values load as 0, while genuine nonnegative integer scores and their persistence keep working. Implementation: add a failing regression test to test/game.test.js that pre-seeds storage with fractional ('1.5'), negative ('-5'), non-finite ('Infinity','NaN'), and malformed ('abc','undefined') values and asserts loadBest returns 0 for each, plus a genuine integer ('5') returns 5 and persists; then fix loadBest in game.js by replacing Number.isFinite(n) with Number.isInteger(n) (which also rejects NaN/Infinity, while n>=0 rejects negatives). Assertions: the regression test plus a task-specific behavioral check (check-bestscore.mjs) verifying each malformed case loads as 0 and genuine integers persist. Verification: run npm test (project check) and node check-bestscore.mjs; obtain independent review before completing.
tasks.title: Task 2 — nonnegative-integer best-score persistence
tasks.acceptance: A new SnakeGame constructed with a store pre-seeded with '1.5', '-5', 'Infinity', 'NaN', 'abc', 'undefined', and '' must report bestScore 0 for each; a store pre-seeded with '5' must report bestScore 5; eating food to score 1 must persist '1' to storage and a new instance reading the same store must load 1. The fix replaces Number.isFinite with Number.isInteger in loadBest, preserving n>=0 for negatives and the existing updateBest persistence.
tasks.current: In game.js loadBest (around line 196): `const n = Number(raw); return Number.isFinite(n) && n >= 0 ? n : 0;` — Number.isFinite(1.5) is true and 1.5>=0, so a fractional stored value like '1.5' loads as 1.5 instead of 0. Number.isFinite already rejects NaN/Infinity, and n>=0 already rejects negatives, but fractional values slip through. Unknown: whether ui.js or any caller reads bestScore as a float (ui.js only renders s.bestScore via textContent, which stringifies fine, so no dependency on it being an integer). The existing tests 'reset returns to a fresh idle state and preserves best score', 'best score persists across instances via shared storage', and 'best score is not reduced by a lower score' pass with integer values.
